packets.responsibility: The single writer for every DOM surface that displays the current stroke/fill colour (`paintStrokeSwatches`/`paintFillSwatches`), plus the two functions that decide which live document field a colour pick should also apply to when the shape is animated in Motion (`routeColorToSelectedMotionRow` for a colour ROW selected in the Motion timeline; `routeColorToMotion` for a shape on canvas with an existing colour track) — so a pick never leaves two colour surfaces disagreeing and never silently misses an animated shape's track.
behavior: 42-line lead-in comment (6156-6197), four parts: (1) 6156-6169, the 2026-07-25 two-writers bug this function exists to fix — `setStrokeColor`/`setFillColor` painted all seven surfaces, the selection handler in `updateUI` hand-wrote only four, measured live on a #8bc34a fill where two right-panel widgets adopted the new colour and two others (the hex field, the LEFT panel) kept showing the stale global colour; (2) 6170-6177, why the selection handler can't just call `setStrokeColor`/`setFillColor` directly (those also APPLY the colour to the selection and would rewrite the object just read, double-pushing undo) and a reminder of the 8-digit-hex `.dataset.hex8` convention (CLAUDE.md §2); (3) 6178-6184, `routeColorToMotion`'s own contract — resolves a Paper item to `(layer index, strokeId)`, guarded on the parent still being in `userLayers` for the same reason `image-mesh-bridge.js`'s `singleRaster()` is (CLAUDE.md §12bis: a `selectedPaths` entry outlives the object it names across `loadFrame`/undo/`importJSON`); (4) 6185-6197, `routeColorToSelectedMotionRow`'s own contract — a colour ROW selected in the Motion timeline is a selection too (2026-08-31, feedback #180: "select couleurs ne prend pas en compte la selection de la propriété"), checked BEFORE the canvas-selection branches and returning `true` when it acted so the two selections can't both fire on one pick (Motion's row is the more specific intent and the only one that can key), delegating all keyframe-vs-static-write logic to `setValue` (motion.js, out of scope).

`routeColorToSelectedMotionRow(prop,hex)` (6198-6210): guard `!window.SMMotion||!SMMotion.selectedColorProps||!SMMotion.writeColorToHolder` returns `false` (6199); `rows=SMMotion.selectedColorProps(prop)` (6200), empty return `false` (6201, the overwhelmingly common non-Motion-selection case, no undo pushed); otherwise `pushUndo()` (6202, BEFORE any write) then `rows.forEach` calling `SMMotion.writeColorToHolder(r.holder,prop,hex)` per matched row, tracking `wrote` (6203-6204); if nothing actually wrote, returns `false` WITHOUT having called `saveActiveLayerFrame`/`updateUI` (6205, still after the `pushUndo()` already ran — an undo entry can be pushed even on this early-return path, since the guard is per-row not per-call); on success, `saveActiveLayerFrame();updateUI();` (6206-6207), conditional `SMEngineBridge.renderNow()` (6208), returns `true` (6209).

`routeColorToMotion(p,prop,hex)` (6211-6217): guards `!p||!p.data||!p.data.strokeId` (6212) and `!window.SMMotion||!SMMotion.writeElementColorFromPicker` (6213) both return `false` with no side effect; `li=userLayers.indexOf(p.parent)` (6214), `li<0` returns `false` (6215, the detached-item guard the lead-in describes); otherwise returns `SMMotion.writeElementColorFromPicker(li,p.data.strokeId,prop,hex)` directly (6216) — no `pushUndo`/`saveActiveLayerFrame`/`updateUI` of its own; the caller (`setStrokeColor`/`setFillColor`, out of scope) always also writes `p.strokeColor`/`p.fillColor=v` itself right after calling this, and owns the undo/save/UI calls for that whole selection loop.

`paintStrokeSwatches(v)` (6218-6224): writes five surfaces unconditionally-or-guarded: `#stroke-well` background (6219, unconditional if the element exists), `#pm-stroke` background (6220, unconditional), `#color-stroke`/`#pm-stroke-c` via `setHex8Input` (6221, app.js:560, out of scope — the paired `.value`/`.dataset.hex8` writer), `#p-stroke-hex` via `hexDisplayValue(v)` guarded by `document.activeElement!==shex` (6222, skips overwriting a field the user is actively typing into), `#p-stroke-alpha` via `alphaPctFromHex(v)` under the same active-element guard (6223).

`paintFillSwatches(v)` (6225-6238): same five-surface shape as the stroke sibling — `#fill-well`/`#pm-fill` backgrounds (6229-6230), `#color-fill`/`#pm-fill-c` via `setHex8Input` (6231), `#p-fill-hex` via `hexDisplayValue` under the active-element guard (6232) — plus a SIXTH surface unique to fill: `#p-opacity` via `alphaPctFromHex(v)`, also active-element-guarded (6237), documented by its own comment (6233-6236) as "now IS the fill's own alpha field" (feedback #48), kept in sync with whatever change just painted the swatch rather than showing a stale percentage. A 2-line comment (6226-6228) explains the background write is unconditional even while fill is disabled, so re-enabling shows the last-picked colour immediately — the `.none` overlay (out of scope) is what communicates "off", not the swatch colour itself.

packets.effects: `routeColorToSelectedMotionRow` reads `SMMotion.selectedColorProps(prop)` (motion.js, out of scope) and writes via `SMMotion.writeColorToHolder` (out of scope) per matched row; on any successful write it calls `pushUndo()`, `saveActiveLayerFrame()`, `updateUI()` and conditionally `SMEngineBridge.renderNow()` — the only one of the four functions in this packet that touches the undo stack, the frame store or a full UI refresh. `routeColorToMotion` reads `p.data.strokeId`/`userLayers.indexOf(p.parent)` and writes via `SMMotion.writeElementColorFromPicker` (out of scope) only — no undo/save/UI call of its own; its caller does that around the whole selection loop. `paintStrokeSwatches`/`paintFillSwatches` read only their own `v` parameter and `document.activeElement`; they write DOM only (`style.background`, `.value`, `.dataset.hex8` via `setHex8Input`) — no state/document/undo mutation, no `saveActiveLayerFrame`/`saveAllLayerFrames` call, safe to call on every repaint.

packets.responsibility: The private, module-scoped memory `reconcileLayerIndexState` (next packet) needs to tell 'the layers shifted under an unchanged index' apart from 'code set a new index on purpose' for every raw-layer-index UI global — never exported on `window`, never read or written outside this packet and the reconciler that consumes it.
behavior: 9-line lead-in comment (6239-6247): documents `renderLayerList`'s own `frameOnly` contract (C19u, out of scope, the next leaf's function) — Animation 2D's rows are frame-INDEPENDENT so a scrub used to rebuild every row for nothing (4.2ms/tick at 40 layers measured), Motion's rows are NOT (each property track prints its value at the playhead), so the decision to skip a full rebuild lives inside `renderLayerList` itself next to its existing mode branch.

28-line lead-in comment continued (6248-6268), the actual rationale for THIS packet's own code: several pieces of UI state hold a raw layer INDEX (`_motionExpandedLayer`, `_perObjBoxes`, `_nvSelectedLayer`, `_motionRevealedLayers`, `_motionRevealedElementLayers`); thirteen different mutation sites (reorder, delete, duplicate, merge, split, undo…) and only two of them remembered to remap any ONE of these globals (dated claim, not independently re-counted by this census — `source_baselines.fixtures`), producing symptoms found while sweeping for the family of bug feedback #798 exposed: the Motion accordion showing another layer's keyframes after a drag-reorder, a video gizmo sitting on whatever slid into a deleted layer's slot. Rather than a 14th ad-hoc remap at each mutation site, the reconciler (next packet) runs ONCE at the single point every mutation already passes through afterwards (`renderLayerList`, via the two calls at 6336-6337). The rule (6263-6268): a global whose value DIFFERS from what was seen last time was written deliberately since (trust it); one whose value is UNCHANGED but now names a different layer has simply been slid under (remap it, by `layerUid` so it survives even an undo's rebuilt layer objects).

`var _idxShadow={};` (6269) — the per-global memory: for a numeric global, `{idx, key}` (the index last seen and the `layerUid` that index named at that time); for an array global, `{arr, keys}` (the array object identity last seen and the per-entry keys it held then).

`_layerKeyOf(ld)` (6270): `return ld?(ld.layerUid||ld):null;` — a layer's stable identity is its `layerUid` when present, else the layer object itself (a fallback that survives only as long as the object reference does, e.g. within one session before an object is rebuilt by `loadFrame`/undo).

`_indexOfLayerKey(key)` (6271-6275): `key==null` returns `-1` (6272); linear scan of `state.layers` matching either object identity (`l===key`) or `l.layerUid===key` (6273), returning the first match's index or `-1` if none found (6274).

No `pushUndo`/`saveActiveLayerFrame`/`renderLayerList` call anywhere in this packet.

packets.responsibility: Applies the remap-vs-trust rule (previous packet's lead-in) to every one of the five named raw-layer-index UI globals — three scalar (`_motionExpandedLayer`, `_perObjBoxes`, `_nvSelectedLayer`) and two array (`_motionRevealedLayers`, `_motionRevealedElementLayers`) — once per call, so a layer reorder/delete/duplicate/merge/split/undo never leaves any of them silently pointing at the wrong layer.
behavior: Scalar globals loop (6277-6288): `['_motionExpandedLayer','_perObjBoxes','_nvSelectedLayer'].forEach(function(name){` — reads `cur=window[name]` (6278) and `sh=_idxShadow[name]` (6279, the previous packet's per-global memory); if `cur` is a number (6280): when the shadow exists, its remembered index equals `cur`, AND the layer currently at `cur` no longer matches the remembered key (6281, `_layerKeyOf(state.layers[cur])!==sh.key`) — the 'slid under an unchanged index' case — remaps via `_indexOfLayerKey(sh.key)` (6282), writing the new index (or `null` if the layer is gone) back onto `window[name]` and re-reading `cur` from it (6283-6284); either way (remapped or not), re-stamps `_idxShadow[name]` with the CURRENT `{idx,key}` pair (6286) so next call's comparison is against this call's result; if `cur` is not a number at all (e.g. `null`/`undefined`), clears the shadow (6287, `_idxShadow[name]=null`) — no reconciliation attempted for a global that isn't currently holding an index.

Array globals loop (6289-6306): `['_motionRevealedLayers','_motionRevealedElementLayers'].forEach(function(name){` — reads `arr=window[name]` (6290) and `sh=_idxShadow[name]` (6291); if `arr` is an Array (6292): when the shadow's remembered array is the SAME object (6293, `sh.arr===arr` — object-identity check, the comment at 6294-6295 explains nobody reassigned it so its entries are index values that may have slid), remaps in place — for each position `i`, resolves the key `k` from the remembered `sh.keys[i]` if that index existed last time, else falls back to `_layerKeyOf(state.layers[arr[i]])` for a brand-new entry (6296-6298), looks up its current index via `_indexOfLayerKey(k)` (6299), and pushes it into `out` only if found AND not already present (`out.indexOf(ni)<0`, 6300 — de-duplicates, since two stale entries could remap onto the same surviving layer); the array is then cleared and replaced in place (`arr.length=0;Array.prototype.push.apply(arr,out);`, 6302) — mutates the SAME array object the caller holds a reference to, rather than reassigning `window[name]`; either way, re-stamps `_idxShadow[name]` with the array's CURRENT identity and per-entry keys (6304, computed fresh from `state.layers[arr[i]]` after the possible remap) so the next call compares against this call's result; if `arr` is not an Array at all, clears the shadow (6305).

packets.effects: Reads and conditionally writes five `window`-scoped globals (`_motionExpandedLayer`, `_perObjBoxes`, `_nvSelectedLayer`, `_motionRevealedLayers`, `_motionRevealedElementLayers`) plus `state.layers` (read-only) and the previous packet's `_idxShadow`/`_layerKeyOf`/`_indexOfLayerKey`. Rebuild loop (6319-6330): `var out=[];` then `_sel.frames.forEach(function(s){` — reads `cur=state.layers[s.layer]` (6321, the layer CURRENTLY at this entry's stored index); if the entry has never been stamped (`s._uid==null`, 6322 — a freshly-added selection entry), stamps `s._uid=_layerKeyOf(cur)` (6323) and keeps it in `out` only if a key was actually resolved (6324, `if(s._uid!=null)out.push(s);`), then returns early for this entry (6325) — no remap attempted on a first-seen entry, only stamping; otherwise, if the layer at the stored index still matches the stamped identity (6327, `_layerKeyOf(cur)===s._uid`), keeps the entry unchanged in `out` and moves to the next; otherwise resolves the entry's CURRENT index via `_indexOfLayerKey(s._uid)` (6328) and, if found, rewrites `s.layer=ni` in place and keeps it (6329) — an entry whose layer is gone entirely (`ni<0`) is silently dropped (not pushed to `out` at all, matching the lead-in's 'dropped when the layer is gone').

Commit only on actual change (6331-6333): compares `out.length!==_sel.frames.length` (a drop happened) OR any `out[i]!==_sel.frames[i]` (an object was filtered/reordered) — only then does it clear `_sel.frames` and replace its contents in place (`_sel.frames.length=0;Array.prototype.push.apply(_sel.frames,out);`, 6332) — mutates the array the rest of the app already holds a reference to, rather than reassigning `_sel.frames`; when nothing changed, `_sel.frames` is left completely untouched (not even re-assigned to an equal-contents array), avoiding any spurious reference change for callers that may compare it by identity.

`routeColorToSelectedMotionRow` calls `pushUndo()` (tweens.js:4741, out of scope) once, BEFORE writing any matched row — even on the rare path where every row's `writeColorToHolder` call ends up returning false and the function returns `false` without saving/rendering, an undo entry may already have been pushed. `routeColorToMotion` and the two paint functions never call `pushUndo`. `routeColorToSelectedMotionRow` reads the MOTION-timeline row selection via `SMMotion.selectedColorProps` (out of scope) — a different selection axis from `selectedPaths` (the canvas selection, read only by this scope's callers, not by this scope itself) and from `_layerSel`/`_sel.frames` (the layer-list/frame-cell selections `reconcileLayerIndexState`/`reconcileFrameSelection` protect). `reconcileFrameSelection` is the one function in this scope that directly mutates a selection: it prunes/remaps `_sel.frames` (tweens.js:210, out of scope) entry-by-entry, dropping any entry whose layer no longer exists and rewriting `.layer` for any entry whose layer merely moved.

`routeColorToSelectedMotionRow`/`routeColorToMotion` exist specifically to keep an animated shape's colour TRACK (motion.js, out of scope) in sync with the plain document field a Paper.js render still reads — the lead-in's own two-writers bug was exactly this class of drift, just for DISPLAY surfaces rather than the track itself. `reconcileLayerIndexState` is consumed by Motion specifically: three of its five globals (`_motionExpandedLayer`, `_motionRevealedLayers`, `_motionRevealedElementLayers`) are Motion-only UI state (accordion expansion, U-reveal sets); `_perObjBoxes`/`_nvSelectedLayer` are shared/Animation-2D-adjacent state (per-element isolation boxes, the selected video gizmo). `reconcileFrameSelection`'s `_sel.frames` is Animation-2D-only (frame-cell selection has no Motion equivalent).

None of this scope's four colour functions or two reconcilers is called from export.js or rive-export.js at the frozen SHA (confirmed: no symbol name appears in either file) — all eight are editor-UI-state-only, with no export-path reader of `_idxShadow`, `_motionExpandedLayer`, `_perObjBoxes`, `_nvSelectedLayer`, `_motionRevealedLayers`, `_motionRevealedElementLayers` or `_sel.frames`.
